clue.text: Doubt mostly about a European broadcaster with power gained in series of calls? It's consumed by loads

indicators.note: about here means the shortened doubt word wraps around everything that follows
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to doubt something is to query it
RTE is the Irish state broadcaster

indicators.note: gained in says the power letter is taken inside the series of calls

parts.note: a round, as a doctor's or postman's round, is a series of calls
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A fussy question about a European radio station and its phone-in calls, ending with a riddle about what gets eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'series of calls' is a round of visits, as a doctor or postman makes, not phone calls. The definition describes a fast-food burger eaten in huge numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast-food burger of that size is eaten by loads of customers, a cryptic description rather than a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Mastery in set employee

definitions.meaning: having a firm hold or control of a subject
a stagehand on a film set who moves equipment

explanation.surface: Someone shows command of their craft while working on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a firm hold or control and a film-crew technician who handles camera rigs and scenery.

clue.text: Neglected issue with a celebrated poem

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A literary critic pairs some overlooked topic with a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' here means offspring, not a topic for debate, so 'Neglected issue' is an uncared-for child.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so a neglected child, a homeless stray youngster, is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Reveal disreputable resort concealing a lot of ugly ground

indicators.note: concealing means the resort word hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

indicators.note: ground, as in ground up, says those letters are broken and reshaped
a lot of means most of the word, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: An exposé about a seedy resort that hides much ugly terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims the last letter from 'ugly' before 'ground' scrambles the rest; 'ground' is the anagram signal, not land.
explanation.definitionFit: To make known something private or secret is a direct synonym for disclose.

clue.text: Newsroom employee brought up worry over unionist linked to extremely grotesque and evasive conduct

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to fret is to worry

indicators.note: extremely points to the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A journalist frets about a union man tied to some grotesque and shifty behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns FRET into TERF in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery used to dodge or deceive is the standard meaning of this word for a ruse or evasion.

clue.text: How one might describe lag before advantage in batsman's unintended shot?

parts.note: a lag is a convict, who is inside, in prison
an edge is an advantage over rivals

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured question about falling behind before gaining the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lag' is slang for a convict, not a delay: a prisoner is described as 'inside'. In cricket an inside edge is the ball glancing off the bat's inner side, often onto the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball clipping the inner side of the bat is an accidental deflection, so it is a shot nobody intended.

clue.text: Is our pub's reason for disorder showing no end of hubbub this?

definitions.text: Is our pub's reason for disorder showing no end of hubbub this?

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the preceding phrase are jumbled
no here means the named letter is left out of the jumbled phrase
end of picks the final letter of the noisy word that follows

explanation.surface: A puzzled drinker asks whether the rowdy din explains the chaos in the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram drops one B, the last letter of 'hubbub', from ISOURPUBSREASON before rearranging. The whole clue doubles as a description of a riotously noisy pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous hilarity and noisy disorder in a pub is what the whole clue pictures, so it works as an extended description.

clue.text: Retail location providing criminal information on rugby player

parts.note: to shop someone is slang for informing on them to the police
a centre is a back-division position in rugby

explanation.surface: A grass informs on a rugby player outside a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is British slang for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall or precinct full of stores is a place for retail, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Segmented item shot on grass from the east surrounding island

parts.note: grape, as in grapeshot, is a type of cannon shot

indicators.note: surrounding says the grass word goes around the island letter
from the east, in an across clue, means read right to left

parts.note: turf is grass

explanation.surface: A gardener notes something lying on the lawn, seen from the east, around an island bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns TURF into FRUT, and 'surrounding' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus fruit splits into wedges when peeled, so it is an item made of segments; a cryptic description.

clue.text: Old Fabian overlooking Western decline

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: Sidney and Beatrice Webb were founders of the Fabian Society

explanation.surface: An old Fabian socialist ignores the West and fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fabian Society is a British socialist group; the Webbs were among its leading early members.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or recede, as a tide does when it goes out, is a synonym for fall off.

clue.text: Club protected by pair once

indicators.note: protected by means the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: A golf club was once guarded by a pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's metal-headed stick is a type of club, an example of the category.

clue.text: Complete division in court?

definitions.meaning: to finish or bring to a close
each half of a tennis court is one side that players change between

explanation.surface: A legal case is finally resolved after a split in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to finish, and also each of the two halves of a tennis court that players switch.

clue.text: Turn to take in food say held back — this food?

indicators.note: to take in says the turn word surrounds the following letters

parts.note: to veer is to turn

indicators.note: held back means the food and example words are read in reverse

parts.note: grub is slang for food
say signals an example, EG

explanation.surface: A cook turns to take in some food that was held back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reverses the food and the example together as one string; the definition 'this food?' leans on the wordplay, which is why the setter adds a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatless patty is the meal the wordplay points to, so 'this food' refers to it.

clue.text: EU tax cited in corrupt form? No scope for uncertainty with it

definitions.text: No scope for uncertainty with it

indicators.note: in corrupt form says the letters of the previous words are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Brussels tax is quoted in garbled form, leaving no room for doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Precision or strict accuracy leaves no room for doubt, so the description fits the noun.

clue.text: Director confronted by broken rule and going round city describing blackmarket activity?

indicators.note: confronted by means the director letter has the rest placed in front of it
going round says the jumbled letters enclose the city code
broken says the letters of the next two words are reassembled

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A film director faces a broken rule and travels round the city, hinting at black-market dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RULE AND to UNLARE, and 'going round' places EC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit trade is kept off the books, so goods and income are never reported to the taxman.

clue.text: Catch special insight by unknown character

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a sixth sense
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone catches a glimpse, thanks to some special insight from a mysterious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to spot it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: At college, charges will be higher

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: At university the fees are going to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like fees but means people in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to a greater level or height is the adverb's sense, matching higher in direction.

clue.text: Fool perhaps putting hand in front of tailless dog

indicators.note: in front of means the hand word comes before the dog word

parts.note: pud is an informal word for a hand, especially a child's

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a dingo is an Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: An idiot puts out a hand towards a dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British fruit-and-cream dessert, so 'Fool perhaps' is an example of a dessert, not a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a whipped fruit dessert, so it is an example of a sweet course.

clue.text: Bar creator encountered in hospital with touch of alcoholism

indicators.note: in means the encountered word goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
met means encountered

indicators.note: touch of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A pub owner was met in hospital showing a hint of alcoholism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a bar of music, so the creator is a composer: Bedřich Smetana, the Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a measure in music, so a creator of bars is a composer, here the Czech one.

clue.text: Pooch severing leg from meat

indicators.note: severing means cutting the leg part off the meat word

parts.note: mutton is meat from a sheep
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A dog bites through the leg bone of a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog, so both words are informal names for a hound.

clue.text: Efficiency shown by favourite replacing male in start

indicators.note: replacing says the favourite word takes the place of the male letter

parts.note: to commence is to start
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A favourite takes a man's place at the outset and proves efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable and getting things done well is the sense shared by skill and productive ability.

clue.text: Restrict Asian by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the answer is pronounced like the Asian word

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand

explanation.surface: Someone is restricted, apparently because they are Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind or tether someone limits their freedom, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Misfortune in work after time is wasted

indicators.note: is wasted means the time letter is removed and lost

parts.note: to till the soil is to work it

explanation.surface: Bad luck at work after time is wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' means work the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or trouble that befalls someone is an old noun sense, as in 'for good or for ...'.

clue.text: Correct legislative body relocating 50% of its membership eastwards

indicators.note: relocating says some letters are moved to another spot
half of the body's letters, its first two, move rightward in this across entry

parts.note: a diet is a parliament, as in Japan's

explanation.surface: A parliament corrects itself by moving half its members eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, the first half of DIET, moves to the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text and fix its errors is a direct synonym for amend.

clue.text: A new detective with net spread about media boss's past

parts.note: tec is short for detective

indicators.note: spread about says the letters are scattered and recombined

parts.note: ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A new detective uses a net to investigate a newspaper editor's history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread about' mixes NET with ED to give EDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's background or history, often plural, is their earlier record, which is what this noun means.

clue.text: Attractive order to reduce taking of a drug?

parts.note: cut is an instruction to reduce
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor's appealing instruction to cut down on a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CUT E, the answer is an order to reduce taking of ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty or endearing in appearance is the everyday sense of attractive.

clue.text: Writer in death all oddly discovered

indicators.note: oddly discovered means the odd-numbered letters are uncovered

explanation.surface: A writer is found in a scene where death is everywhere, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Roald Dahl wrote macabre tales, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl is a famous author of children's books and dark short stories, an example of a writer.

clue.text: A lecher getting excited with scant hint of right embracing daughter?

definitions.text: A lecher getting excited with scant hint of right embracing daughter?

indicators.note: embracing says the jumbled letters wrap around the daughter letter
getting excited says the letters are stirred into a new order
hint of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A lustful man becomes aroused, with little sense of right, while hugging a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting excited' jumbles A LECHER SCANT to CRALESNATCHE; 'embracing' puts D inside, and R ends it. The whole clue also pictures such a man.
explanation.definitionFit: This hyphenated phrase is slang for someone who dates a much younger partner, which a lecher with a daughter-aged lover is.
